key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:Typhoon-Thompson:0:01E4
name: unpack_block_backwards
description: Decodes a bit-packed stream into a buffer that is filled from its end toward its start, writing literal bytes and copying earlier output for back-references. It restarts the decode from the beginning when a particular control value is reached.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:Typhoon-Thompson:0:01EC
name: resume_packed_stream_decode
description: Continues the same bit-packed decoding as the block unpacker, starting with a back-reference copy and then making literal or match decisions. It returns an error value if the output pointer runs past the buffer limit.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:Typhoon-Thompson:0:020E
name: unpack_bitstream_short_copy
description: Runs the bit-packed decoder with a short-copy path that advances the output by a small fixed amount for certain control values. The routine writes decoded bytes backwards into the output buffer and ends when the bit stream is exhausted.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:Typhoon-Thompson:0:023C
name: cycle_color_register_values
description: Writes a 16-bit counter that counts down through every possible value to the color register, one value per iteration. The loop runs through all 65536 values and then returns.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:s/type:0:0136
name: copy_block_and_call_handler
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a structure to a destination pointer, but only when that pointer is set. It then calls through a stored routine pointer.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0000
name: start_program_and_relocate
description: Serves as the program entry point. It calls the exec library to open the system library, clears the interrupt and DMA enable registers, copies a block of its own code into low memory, and then installs a trap handler and issues trap 0.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0020
name: store_status_word
description: Copies the global status word into a second global variable so that later routines can read the same value.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:002A
name: probe_memory_type_flags
description: Calls the exec memory-type query three times and sets one byte of a global flag word to all ones for each call that returns a nonzero result. Flags for calls that return zero stay clear.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0070
name: call_exec_function_pair
description: Calls two exec library functions in sequence from the exec base and then returns. The register and interrupt effects listed for this routine come from those library functions rather than from the routine's own code.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:00FE
name: copy_words_and_patch_nops
description: Copies a block of words from a source to a destination, then calls a fixed routine. When a global flag is set, it overwrites two words of memory with no-operation codes before issuing trap 0.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0144
name: open_named_file_store_handle
description: Opens a file using the name text referenced by the routine, stores the returned handle in a global variable, and then makes two further library calls at fixed offsets.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0204
name: decode_and_expand_runs
description: Runs a bit-driven decoder that fills a buffer from its end toward its start with literals and back-references. It then expands run-length markers into the output area until a fixed end address and issues trap 0.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:02FA
name: shift_bit_buffer_store_byte
description: Stores the low byte of the current bit buffer word into a memory location, then returns the buffer shifted right by one with its top bit set. This is the step that advances the bit reader's state.

key: typhoon thompson (1989)(broderbund)[cr qtx][t +1 miracle]/Typhoon Thompson (1989)(Broderbund)[cr QTX][t +1 Miracle].adf:nor:0:0314
name: skip_bits_with_refill
description: Shifts a bit buffer right by a given count, calling the refill routine each time the buffer empties so that the next word is loaded.

name: install_trap_zero_and_trap
description: Writes this routine's own address into the trap-0 vector and then issues trap 0, handing execution to that handler. The code contains nothing else.

name: enable_dma_and_start_copper
description: Clears the DMA and interrupt state, enables selected DMA channels and interrupts, and starts the copper list through the copper subroutine. It returns zero.

name: save_dma_interrupt_state
description: Saves two copies of a status word with its top bit set into two globals, keeping the DMA and interrupt enable state so it can be restored later.

name: restore_dma_interrupt_state
description: Writes the two saved state words back to the DMA and interrupt enable registers, one after the other.

name: set_buffer_pointer_clear_field
description: Stores the address of a global buffer into a field of a structure addressed by the base register, then clears a second field of that structure.

name: initialize_three_table_entries
description: Writes three constant words into fixed memory locations, each stored four bytes after a count of three. This sets up three entries of a small table.

name: poll_joystick_button_state
description: Waits for a status byte to clear, samples the joystick and button inputs through five subroutine calls, and returns once the sampled bits show the button state it is looking for. Otherwise it sets the global result to all ones.

name: countdown_with_reload
description: Counts a global value down while it is nonzero. When it is already zero, it calls a routine and decrements again, and if the value reaches zero it reloads it with eight and calls another routine.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two other routines one after the other and then returns. It has no logic of its own, so the work is done by the two callees.

name: configure_blit_from_position
description: Computes a source address from a position, using a row stride of forty bytes, and programs the blitter with it along with a fixed destination address, modulo values, mask words, a control word and a blit size.

name: lookup_character_offset
description: Reads the next character from a string and stores a value in a global. For the letter s it stores a fixed constant; for other characters it scans a second string in steps of sixteen to find the character and stores the resulting offset.

name: start_fixed_blit_after_idle
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, then programs it with two fixed source and destination addresses, two modulo values, full mask words, a copy control word and a blit size.

name: start_blit_to_saved_pointer
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, then programs it with the address held in a global variable as the destination, a fixed modulo, mask words, a control word and a blit size.

name: blit_tile_grid_from_table
description: Waits for the blitter, then loops over a grid of twenty-two rows of sixteen cells. For each cell it computes source and destination addresses from a table value and an offset and starts a blit of fixed size, resetting the table pointer to a fixed address when it falls below a threshold.

name: swap_buffer_pointer_pair
description: Switches a global between two fixed buffer addresses and writes the chosen address, and the address forty bytes after it, into two pointer pairs as high and low words.

name: copy_next_char_with_offset
description: Reads the next byte of a text pointer, restarting at a fixed text address when the end marker is reached, and stores that byte at one location and the byte raised by thirty-two at another.

name: free_memory_and_clear_slot
description: Calls a subroutine and a function pointer, calls the system memory-free function through a global, and zeroes a longword just before a pointer. It then returns the two register values.

name: unpack_stream_with_table_updates
description: Decodes a packed stream into a buffer filled from its end toward its start. The codes it reads repeat bytes, copy earlier output, or add a value into a table of words, and a support routine is called through a function pointer to move data.

name: select_half_or_input_word
description: Returns half of a second word when a flag equals one, otherwise returns the input word unchanged.

name: mask_word_with_table_entry
description: Looks up a word in a fixed table using an index passed in a register, and returns it ANDed with the input word.

name: wait_for_port_then_reply
description: Finds the current task and, when its message-port field is empty, waits on the port and fetches a message. It then calls a processing routine and, if a message was obtained, forbids task switching and replies to it.

name: wait_for_flag_then_halt
description: Busy-waits until a global flag becomes all ones, then enters an endless loop that never returns.

name: copy_block_find_table_base
description: Copies a block of longwords from an offset inside a larger area into the global area and checks a tag value, copying one byte when it matches. It then finds the largest word in a table of four-byte entries, computes a base address from it, and fills fourteen entries with addresses stepping by a stride.

name: initialize_system_and_idle
description: Clears a small block of state, sets up several global words and writes DMA and interrupt enable values. It then scales a table of words by four, runs a setup loop, and ends in an endless wait loop.

name: set_flag_then_initialize_system
description: Sets bits in a flag byte inside the base-addressed block, then runs the same setup as the segment entry: it clears state, writes DMA and interrupt enable values, scales a table, and ends in an endless wait loop.

name: toggle_nop_code_patches
description: Swaps two sets of instruction words between their patched and original forms, using a state byte to choose which form is written. It then clears the state byte and returns a value derived from the input registers.

name: toggle_keyboard_code_patches
description: Switches two code patch sites between no-operation and original instruction words, selected by a state byte, then clears the state byte. It returns a value derived from the input registers.

name: write_patch_word_and_toggle
description: Writes a fixed instruction word to a location, then toggles a second instruction word between a no-operation and its original form when the state byte matches. It clears the state byte and returns a value derived from the input registers.

name: write_on_state_patch_words
description: Writes two fixed instruction words to a location and clears the state byte, then returns a value derived from the input registers. The surrounding facts show interrupt and library calls and text labelled on and off, which are not in this pseudo-code.

name: advance_table_on_timer
description: Counts a delay timer down and, when it expires, resets it and advances a pointer through a table of words, wrapping at the end. It stores the current word to a global variable and calls two subroutines.

name: copy_glyph_to_two_rows
description: Looks up a character code in a table of up to seventy-three codes, then copies its eight glyph bytes to two destinations a fixed distance apart, one row per byte. It advances through the text string as each character is drawn.

name: rotate_points_and_start_blit
description: Swaps two buffer pointers, then computes rotated and offset coordinates for eleven pairs of table entries using fixed-point multiplication and stores them. It waits for the blitter to be idle and then starts a blit of fixed size.

name: reset_blitter_masks_and_modulo
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, then writes full first and last mask words, a control word and two modulo values for the blitter.

name: build_row_offset_table
description: Fills 256 consecutive words with offsets that increase by forty for each row, forming a lookup table of row start positions.

name: draw_line_with_blitter
description: Orders two endpoints, computes the step counts and octant of a line, toggles one pixel bit at the start position, and programs the blitter with the modulo, control and size values to draw the line.

name: set_bit_refill_random_table
description: Sets one bit in a byte, then fills sixteen longwords by repeatedly rotating a state word, adding a constant and exclusive-ORing another. It decrements several byte counters and sets flags when they reach zero.

name: dispatch_sound_command
description: Dispatches on the low two bits of its input. A zero value advances the sound state and updates channel timers, a one value starts a music sequence by setting channel pointers and volumes, a two value stores a value, and a three value initializes one of four audio channels from a table.

name: initialize_channel_structure
description: Clears several fields of a channel structure, stores a pointer taken from a second structure, and sets a fixed longword, a mask byte and a flag byte.

name: generate_pseudo_random_sequence
description: Fills sixteen longwords by repeatedly rotating a state word, adding a constant and exclusive-ORing another, while decrementing several byte counters and setting flags when they reach zero.

name: step_music_channel_sequence
description: Reads the next sequence event for one channel, loading its instrument and state from data tables, and updates the channel's pitch and volume counters. It calls a per-effect routine through a jump table and wraps the sequence position at the end of its data.

name: store_nibble_and_mask_return
description: Stores the low four bits of its second input into a field of the structure, and returns the first input with a fixed set of bits turned on.

name: store_low_nibble_field
description: Stores the low four bits of its input into a byte field of the structure addressed by the base register.

name: set_or_clear_global_bit
description: Sets bit one of a global byte when the input is zero, and clears that bit otherwise.

name: store_negated_low_byte
description: Stores the negated low byte of its input into a word field of the structure addressed by the base register.

name: store_low_byte_word_field
description: Stores the low byte of its input into a word field of the structure addressed by the base register.

name: store_input_byte_field
description: Stores the input byte into a fixed byte field of the structure addressed by the base register.

name: store_low_six_bits_field
description: Stores the low six bits of its input into a byte field of the structure addressed by the first address register.

name: store_six_bits_at_base
description: Stores the low six bits of its input into a byte field of the block addressed by the base register.

name: store_table_pointer
description: Masks its input to six bits, multiplies it by sixteen, adds a fixed base address, and stores the result as a pointer in a structure field.

name: boot_block_setup_interrupts
description: The decompiled code is unavailable, so this describes the listed facts only. The routine is the boot block entry, calls the exec forbid function, writes to the interrupt registers and the color register, and calls three other routines.

name: capture_pending_interrupt_bits
description: When the interrupt master-enable bit is set, it stores the bits common to the interrupt enable and request registers, masked to their low fourteen bits, in a global variable. It returns its input value unchanged.

name: read_mfm_track_sectors
description: Sets a bit mask and a drive port byte, then decodes sector words by combining alternating bits with a mask for MFM decoding. When the decoded value matches, it programs the disk controller with the MFM sync word, a DMA pointer and length, and waits for the interrupt request bit.

name: pulse_control_port_bits
description: Writes six byte values to a control port, each clearing one of five bits in turn and then restoring all bits. It is a fixed sequence of pulses that takes no data input.

name: wait_status_bit_then_clear
description: Loops while a status bit on a port is set, calling a subroutine on each pass. When the bit clears, it zeroes a word field of the structure addressed by the second register.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Moves a stored position toward the input value, one step per unit of difference, by writing alternating control port values with a fixed delay between steps. It calls a subroutine first when the stored position is negative.

name: pulse_control_port_repeatedly
description: Repeats a two-stage port write for the count in its input, with a fixed delay after each pair. The two writes differ in one bit, so each pass produces a single pulse.

name: store_params_and_loop_calls
description: Stores two register inputs into structure fields, then calls subroutines once per count in a loop, setting a field to two on each pass before the calls.

name: read_mfm_sector_with_retries
description: Starts a disk read DMA with the MFM sync word and a fixed buffer address, waits for the read to finish, then searches for the sync word and decodes an MFM sector while checking its checksum. It retries up to ten times when the check fails.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiled code is only a bad-instruction marker that halts the decoder, so the routine has no behaviour of its own.

name: copy_doubled_table_when_flagged
description: When a status bit is set, it clears a flag word, advances two counters and calls a subroutine. If a pointer is set, it copies sixteen table words into a fixed area with each value doubled, then clears four longwords and restores the flag bit.

name: fill_ramp_or_load_lookup
description: When a state word matches a fixed value, it either fills a 32-entry byte table with ascending values followed by a terminator, or loads three bytes from a lookup table indexed by the state.

name: rotate_and_lookup_table_entry
description: When the input is nonzero, it rotates the value right by one bit, xors the high byte with a constant, and uses the result to look up a byte in a fixed table. It stores the looked-up byte with a flag bit as the global result, and zeroes the result when the input is zero.

name: store_sum_pair_with_carry
description: When the input pointer is not the special value two, it computes a sum from the input and a constant, then stores that sum in two consecutive words with the carry from the first addition included. It clears the global result afterwards.

name: clamp_halved_scaled_value
description: When the input equals one, it halves the value, subtracts a fixed offset and clamps it to a range twice. It sets the global to all ones when neither clamp applied, and to zero otherwise.

name: set_status_to_all_ones
description: Stores the all-ones value in a global variable and returns.

name: accumulate_signed_counter_deltas
description: Sets two bits of a status byte when a per-channel flag is nonzero, then negates and adds the channel input into two accumulator words, clearing the per-channel flag each time. The result is a pair of signed running totals.

name: decode_joystick_direction_deltas
description: Decodes joystick direction bits from its input word into signed x and y deltas and adds them to two accumulator words. It sets a status bit when bit seven of the input is clear.

name: decode_mouse_movement_deltas
description: Sets two button status bits when their input bits are clear, then adds the signed movement fields of the input word into two accumulator words.

name: dispatch_by_input_flags
description: Reads a flag byte and stores a two-bit value derived from it, setting the global to all ones when either of the low two bits is set. When either of two stored pointers is set, it calls a routine selected from a table by that value.

name: enable_dma_or_clear_state
description: When the input is zero, it writes a DMA enable value, then calls a stored routine pointer several times with subroutine calls between. Otherwise it clears four global words.

name: set_audio_channel_defaults
description: Stores fixed default values for two audio channel periods and a pointer to the global block. The routine has no branching.

name: stub_return_only
description: The routine contains only a return and does nothing.

name: find_highest_bit_table_entry
description: When the input byte is nonzero, it scans from bit seven downward for the highest set bit, then loads a longword from a table indexed by that bit number. Otherwise it leaves the global unchanged.

name: load_channel_record_fields
description: Sets two state words to one, loads several fields from a fourteen-byte record in a table selected by a value, and stores a pointer to the global block.

name: clear_channel_bits_and_store
description: Clears bits in the global control word and, if a selected bit of the input is set, stores fixed values and a routine pointer into state words. It then zeroes the global result.

name: set_indexed_bit_and_call
description: Sets the bit numbered by the low three bits of the global value in a byte, then calls a subroutine.

name: find_highest_bit_second_table
description: When the input byte is nonzero, it finds the highest set bit by scanning from bit seven downward, then loads a longword from a second table indexed by that bit number. Otherwise it leaves the global unchanged.

name: load_second_channel_record
description: Sets two state words, then loads several fields from a fourteen-byte record selected by the state value and stores a pointer to the global block.

name: clear_channel_bits_store_two
description: Clears bits in the global control word and, if a selected bit of the input is set, stores a value of two, a value and a routine pointer into state words. It then zeroes the global result.

name: set_mask_bit_and_call
description: Sets the bit numbered by the low three bits of the global value in a byte, then calls a subroutine.

name: stub_return_only
description: The routine contains only a return and does nothing.

name: stub_return_only
description: The routine contains only a return and does nothing.
